reason: Written 2026-11-11 before any role was computed. The gain the next tier up must show before a role leaves a tier, in shares of the better model's score on the kind's evaluations (0 to 1): twice the 5 percent tolerance the tier chooser already allows for benchmark noise, because the evaluations publish no interval in our data. The full threshold is base_gain x frequency factor x price premium / stakes factor.

The price premium is log2 of the next tier's list price (input plus output USD per million tokens, the price row in force that day) over this tier's, never below 1: every doubling of price asks for the base gain once more, and a step that costs less than double asks for it once. List prices come from the tier prices file, never from a name in code.
The metric climbs the ladder only as far as quality. Best is never reached by the metric: it is set by a person or by the structure watch (the constraint best_only_on_request_or_watch).

If this rule is wrong it is changed in a new recorded row with its date and the reason, with the table recomputed once; it is never retuned to move a role. This metric family was retuned after seeing results three times and that is a recorded weakness.

Today one ladder for every kind: fast, balanced, quality, in this order, each tier filled by the model the tier choice names that day. A kind or a role may later carry its own ladder rows (a ladder row with a kind or role set replaces this one for it, the way a role variant replaces a tier's weights in tier_metrics.csv), so a type of task can have its own tiers.
Second rung.
Top rung the metric reaches.

More than four calls in a turn or a run, or one call per item over many items (per file, per search, per step of a run). Many calls multiply the cost of a dearer tier and are the owner's reason for fast, so the gain asked for doubles.
One to four calls in a turn or a run. The reference.

Fewer than one call per turn or run (on a condition, a schedule or a request). The owner allows a higher tier for an infrequent call that shows a significant improvement, so half the gain is asked for.
An error stays inside the call: a later step, a validator or the call's own metric catches it. Divides nothing.
An error changes what the turn does or says. The owner's reason for balanced: a significant downstream effect for the turn, so half the gain is asked for.
An error persists in records, structure or the design of an arm. The owner's reason for quality: a quarter of the gain is asked for.
Structured workflow completion on declared inputs: the nearest public evaluation to choosing a label from facts. No public evaluation measures classification on current models, so it is a proxy.
Abstaining instead of inventing: a label must not be invented. A proxy for the same reason.
Structured tool and workflow completion: gathering is reading, filtering and ranking records through connected tools and files.
Not inventing: gathered material must be what the sources say, and a gather call that invents misleads every later call.
Short factual answers: a proxy for picking the right item from many.
Structured tool and workflow completion: orchestrating is choosing steps, arguments and routes for connected tools.
A plan or an extraction must not invent facts or arguments.
Multi-step agentic completion: a proxy for a plan that holds across steps; it measures running a plan, not choosing one.
Agentic work in a terminal: the work the main session and its sub-agents do.
Real repository changes: file editing and change work.
Tool use against connected systems: operations on connected systems.
Knowledge-work agent tasks (Elo): a proxy for work that is not code.
Expert-level reasoning: a reviewer must see what a non-expert misses. Proxy: it grades answers, not reviews.
Research-level reasoning: a proxy for judging a hard claim.
Knowledge-work agent tasks (Elo): a proxy for judging a work product against a brief.
A reviewer must not invent flaws or pass an invented claim.
Expert-judged work products (Elo): the nearest public measure of prose a person reads and judges.
Prose a person reads must not state invented facts.
Expert-level reasoning: structure work is judged by experts. A proxy: it grades answers.
Research-level reasoning.
Long knowledge-work agent tasks (Elo): multi-step deliverables, the shape of structure work.
Long-horizon agentic work.
Long-horizon code: records and arms are code and specification changes.

Classification is fast tier only, always (the owner's hard rule, kept as a recorded constraint): a classification prompt is improved by training on past cases on the fast tier, not by buying a larger model, and the calls are many. An explicit tier from a person does not change it.
Any response a person reads is at least balanced (the owner's rule): a person reads the error directly, so the lowest tier is not allowed for prose a person reads.

Balanced is the default for deep work (the owner's stated rule of 2026-11-10), added 2026-11-11 after the first computation showed the metric alone picking quality for this role; the row still shows that pick and its numbers so the disagreement stays visible. A person's explicit tier still wins (the role lets a person set it). The roles that follow the main session keep following it.

Best only where a person asks for it or sets it, plus the structure watch (the owner's rule): the watch is the one small call that guards structural risk, so it runs on the best tier without being asked. The metric never reaches best.
